title: Claude redelivery during a slow start build
summary: Checks whether a real Claude redelivery around the first spawn lease reuses the same QA workspace without a stale nack. A separate instrumented variant holds the local first-attempt nack past the provider lease while preserving the advertised budget.
prerequisites: Use clean coder/agent-relay main for F1a. For F1b, pin that same main commit plus an explicitly QA-only, uncommitted source mutation, and record its exact git diff and SHA-256 alongside the build command, binary hash and launched path.

Confirm the steven QA-only Claude pool, the dedicated provisioner and a new QA template version with a cancellable eight-minute start-build delay. No unrelated QA workspaces or provider requests may be active.

Keep decoded debug work-order claims and raw Relay logs private. Publish only reviewed timestamps, attempt numbers and redacted claim comparisons; never publish work-order JWTs, provider session IDs or credentials.
Anthropic controls redelivery. Observe its actual attempt, iat and exp rather than assuming a new budget or asserting that a second work order arrives at exactly T+4:50.

Q11-F1b.qa_source_mutation: Only qa-claude attempt 0's local build watcher waits 60s past its original deadline; provider expected_spawn_seconds remains 300 and attempt 1 retains its own unmodified deadline. The exact patch is run evidence.

variants.title: Redelivery before the first deadline
variants.summary: With one slow Claude QA build, checks whether a provider redelivery near T+4:50 takes the same workspace and supersedes the first watcher. A fresh or stale redelivery budget changes the expected branch; a missing redelivery blocks the live check.

steps.action: Verify the new template and latest-main Relay candidate. With a short QA-only build delay, confirm the provisioner can cancel a pending disposable start build; record status and cleanup before enabling the eight-minute delay.
steps.expected: A short delayed QA build starts, the cancellation request is recorded and the job settles promptly with canceled_at set. A running Terraform apply may finish with job status failed; both QA pools remain healthy after cleanup.
steps.evidence: Template version, binary provenance, redacted provisioner event times, canceled_at, terminal job status and cleanup.

steps.action: Start one benign Claude QA conversation. Capture attempt 0's verified iat and exp privately, its claim time and workspace/build 1, then poll the eight-minute build without manually triggering a second provider request.
steps.expected: One QA workspace and a slow first start build are present. No runner is serving while the build waits.
steps.evidence: Redacted attempt 0 claim and workspace/build pseudonyms, issue/expiry times, build-delay marker and status polls.

steps.action: Observe for an Anthropic redelivery near T+4:50. Compare attempt 1's verified iat and exp with attempt 0 in private debug logs; derive the actual second deadline as min(iat plus 5m, exp).
steps.expected: If attempt 1 arrives with a fresh remaining budget, follow branch A. If its budget is already exhausted, record branch B without calling it an unconditional product failure. If no redelivery arrives, mark the live scenario blocked.
steps.evidence: Redacted attempt, issue/expiry comparisons, provider observation bounds and derived deadline; no raw work-order payload.

steps.action: For a fresh-budget redelivery, observe workspace dedupe, cancellation and settlement of build 1, then start build 2 on the same workspace. Check that watcher 1 does not nack or delete the replacement.
steps.expected: No second workspace; build 1 stops and reaches terminal canceled or failed with canceled_at set, build 2 waits again, and attempt 0 is superseded without a stale nack. Record race ordering if watcher 1 acquires the lock first.
steps.evidence: Redacted workspace/build correlation, cancellation and rebuild event times, both attempt-specific nack counts and applied outcomes.

steps.action: Watch through the actual attempt 1 deadline and cleanup. If the second eight-minute build still runs, observe its terminal nack, cancellation and deletion; capture the provider outcome and restore the QA config.
steps.expected: Only the current attempt can receive a terminal nack at its own deadline. After cancellation, the current build reaches terminal canceled or failed with canceled_at set, then the QA workspace is deleted; a completed build before deadline is a separate success observation.
steps.evidence: Sourced Relay/Coder/provider timeline, redacted debug excerpt, QA-only cleanup and visually reviewed screenshot crops.

cleanup: Keep the new template's zero-delay default, remove the F1a pool delay and debug overlay, and verify both QA pool-health gauges and no leftover QA workspace.
Preserve private raw logs and original screenshots outside the public repository. Publish only sanitized evidence and the exact source commit and SHA-256 of the binary actually used.

variants.title: Observe lease-expiry re-offer with a delayed local nack
variants.summary: Advertises a five-minute Claude spawn lease while an instrumented QA-only first watcher waits one extra minute. Checks whether a real provider re-offer arrives at lease expiry, reconciles the original workspace and supersedes its watcher; missing redelivery blocks this instrumented check.

steps.action: Confirm only the QA-only first-attempt watcher gains 60 seconds, while the advertised lease and subsequent attempt deadline remain unchanged. Pin the clean base commit, exact uncommitted source diff, binary SHA-256, restored baseline config and QA-only template version before applying the 5m/480s debug overlay.
steps.expected: The QA Relay is healthy in both pools with expected_spawn_seconds 300 for Claude, one QA-only slow-build template, and no existing QA workspaces. No production source or pool is modified.
steps.evidence: Source patch, patch hash, binary and overlay hashes, template version, redacted readiness, pool and workspace counts.

steps.action: Send one benign prompt in a new Claude conversation using the confirmed Steven-Testing environment. Observe signed attempt 0 iat/exp privately and its sole delayed build, then watch at least through its provider lease expiry without manually retrying or nacking.
steps.expected: The first QA workspace has one unfinished 480-second start build; no runner registered or first-attempt nack occurred before the five-minute lease. A provider re-offer is possible but must be observed, not inferred.
steps.evidence: Bounded prompt observation, attempt-0 timestamps, build-delay marker, status polls and redacted first-attempt nack count.

steps.action: Watch for an actual attempt 1 through the 60-second local observation grace and compare its verified iat/exp with attempt 0. If it has a usable budget, track cancellation of build 1 and build 2 on the same workspace across the old watcher deadline; otherwise report the actual branch or missing prerequisite.
steps.expected: A fresh-budget re-offer uses one workspace and supersedes watcher 1 without its stale nack or deletion; a stale or absent re-offer is recorded honestly, not called a clean-main product failure. The second deadline is min(attempt-1 iat plus 5m, exp).
steps.evidence: Redacted attempt numbers and claim times, workspace/build pseudonyms, cancellation and supersession logs, per-attempt applied nack counts and observation bounds.

steps.action: Observe the current build through its actual deadline and natural QA cleanup, then restore the safe config and original unmodified QA binary. Verify readiness, both pool-health gauges and no QA template workspaces. Keep raw payloads and full screenshots private.
steps.expected: Only the current work order receives any terminal nack at its own deadline, canceled_at and terminal job status are recorded, and the sole QA workspace is absent. A failure to re-offer instead settles as a blocked redelivery assertion with cleanup fully verified.
steps.evidence: Sourced Relay/Coder/provider event timeline, sanitized log excerpt and image crops, exact source diff, restoration and cleanup checks.

cleanup: Restore the original mode-0600 safe QA config and prior unmodified launcher binary after the test. Keep the published template's delay default 0 and leave no QA workspace.
Never publish private work-order payloads, credentials, raw logs or unreviewed screenshots. Record the binary actually run, its clean base commit and the exact uncommitted QA-only git diff.

notes: A second work order cannot be synthesized by sending another browser prompt. Provider iat/exp and actual redelivery time decide the live branch; do not pin branch A without evidence.

A canceled running Terraform apply can be labeled failed by Coder even with canceled_at set. Judge cancellation by the recorded request, terminal job status, no duplicate workspace and no stale nack, not by the canceled label alone.
The long delay intentionally prevents either start build from finishing inside a five-minute spawn budget. A different faster second-build success path needs a separate case.
Do not run Cursor, change shared dogfood pools, publish raw debug payloads, or assume an HTTP nack was applied merely because a request was sent.
